scope: Hand-curated template library of peptide linkers that have actually been used in engineered fusion proteins, labelled on two property axes (cleavability, rigidity) with a per-entry citation. This is a TEMPLATE library for conditioning/retrieval, not a function-tested dataset: see reports/EXPERIMENTALLY_TESTED_LINKER_SOURCE_SEARCH_2026-10-12.md for why those are different tiers of evidence and why no count from this file may be presented as function-tested linker measurements.

rigidity.flexible: The cited source places the sequence in a flexible-linker category, or states it adopts no stable secondary structure.
rigidity.rigid: The cited source places the sequence in a rigid-linker category (alpha-helical or Pro-rich).
rigidity.unassigned: The cited source does not place the sequence on the flexible/rigid axis at all. Unassigned is NOT a third class and must never be silently converted to flexible.

cleavability.cleavable: The cited source identifies a protease, reducing, or otherwise scissile element in the sequence and reports it being cleaved in a fusion-protein context.
cleavability.non_cleavable: Used as a stable connector; see each entry's cleavability.basis for whether this was stated by the source or inferred from category exclusion.
cleavability.unassigned: Not determinable from the cited source.

basis_codes.source_category: The source's own section/table heading assigns this label.
basis_codes.source_stated: The source states the property for this sequence in text.
basis_codes.inferred_from_category_exclusion: INFERENCE by this project: the source lists the entry under a non-cleavable category and names no scissile element. Weaker than source_stated.
basis_codes.not_stated: The source is silent; label is 'unassigned'.

chen2013.text_used: Full text retrieved 2026-10-17 from the copy filed at https://ptacts.uspto.gov/ptacts/public-informations/petitions/1550906/download-documents?artifactId=N6qLOycdwIeNhULZPLK93YMckJGHSTN_JCECUMgo6sKL3aNHsHyMktI because pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov served a reCAPTCHA interstitial to this environment.
chen2013.role: Primary curation source for every entry in this file. Category assignments are this review's own section and table headings.
internal_inconsistencies_noted: Table 4 prints the (H4)2 helical linker as -LEA(EAAAK)4ALEA(EAAAK)4ALE- while the main text prints A(EAAAK)4ALEA(EAAAK)4A.
Fig. 3 prints A(EAAAAK)4ALEA(EAAAAK)4A with five alanines, conflicting with the EAAAK repeat used elsewhere in the same review.
The virus coat protein display linker is cited as reference [51] in text and [50] in Table 3.
Fig. 4 cites [58], [66], [67] where the text cites [59], [64], [68] for the same cleavable examples.

george2002.citation: George RA, Heringa J. An analysis of protein domain linkers: their classification and role in protein folding. Protein Engineering 15 (2002) 871-879.
george2002.role: Cited for the natural-linker classification axis and as the paper behind LinkerDB. No row-level LinkerDB records are in this repository; see acquisition_status.
george2002.label_axis_provided: helicity (LinkerDB splits natural linkers at >30% vs <30% helical residues), which is NOT the same axis as engineered rigid/flexible design intent and must not be merged with it
george2002.text_used: LinkerDB interface page read 2026-10-17. The page confirms four categories (1-linker, Helical >30% helical, Non-helical <30% helical, All linkers), a query interface, and download links for All/Helical-type/Extended-type.

hubbard1994.citation: Hubbard SJ, Eisenmenger F, Thornton JM. Modeling studies of the change in conformation required for cleavage of limited proteolytic sites. Protein Science 3 (1994).
hubbard1994.role: Evidence that limited-proteolysis sites require a local conformational change, which is why a scissile site and a stable helix cannot occupy the same residues.
hubbard1994.text_used: Citation metadata verified from the publisher listing on 2026-10-17; volume and page range not confirmed and full text not read here. Cite for the general requirement of local unfolding at cleavage sites, not for any specific numeric claim.

thrombin_helix_unfolding.citation: Protein unfolding is essential for cleavage within the alpha-helix of a model protein substrate by the serine protease, thrombin.
thrombin_helix_unfolding.role: Direct experimental support for rigid-plus-cleavable incompatibility: a scissile bond inside an alpha-helix is not cleaved until the helix unfolds.
thrombin_helix_unfolding.text_used: Title and publisher listing seen 2026-10-17; abstract page only. Author list, year and journal NOT verified. Do not place in a manuscript bibliography until resolved.

acquisition_status.linkerdb: NOT ACQUIRED. LinkerDB is live at https://ibi.vu.nl/programs/linkerdbwww and offers bulk downloads, but this container's egress allowlist denies ibi.vu.nl and the page's download hrefs are not recoverable through the fetch tool available here. Nothing from LinkerDB is in this file. Its natural-linker helicity labels are the most promising route to a labelled set larger than this template library, so acquiring it is the top data task.
acquisition_status.synlinker: NOT ACQUIRED and likely defunct. The SynLinker home page (about 2,150 natural plus about 110 empirical/engineered linkers, searchable by protease sensitivity) states it changed URL in March 2016 without giving the new address. This matches literature/LINKER_MOTIF_DISCOVERY_SURVEY_2026-10-12.md. Do not manufacture records from its advertised counts.

composite_templates.construction: Two parts, not one segment: a rigid spacer (helical EAAAK repeat or Pro-rich) carrying length and orientation, plus a short flexible protease cassette (the scissile motif padded with Gly/Ser) placed at one end rather than inside the rigid element.

parts.contributes: the scissile site plus the local backbone freedom it needs

composite_templates.rationale: A scissile bond needs local backbone freedom to reach a protease active site. An alpha-helix is the opposite of that, so a protease site inside a helical spacer does not yield a cleavable rigid linker; it yields a rigid linker that is not cleaved until something unfolds it. The two properties must occupy different residues of the same construct.
evidence: hubbard1994: limited-proteolysis sites require a local conformational change before cleavage.
thrombin_helix_unfolding: a scissile bond inside an alpha-helix is cleaved only after the helix unfolds.

chen2013, entry cleav-mmp-plglwa: the review's own MMP-cleavable construct places the PLGLWA motif BETWEEN two GGGGS sequences, so the composite pattern is already standard practice for the flexible case.
chen2013, absence: the review lists no construct combining an EAAAK-type helical spacer with a protease site, although it covers both at length.

attribution_note: Each entry's attributed_origin is the primary work the review credits, as the review credits it. Where a DOI appears it was independently verified; where it is null the attribution is recorded at review-level only and must be cited as 'Chen et al. 2013, attributing to <author year>'. Do not upgrade a null DOI to a citation without checking the primary paper.
